*Kilesagocchaka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.12) is a section of the *Paṭṭhāna*, the seventh and final treatise of the canonical Abhidhamma Piṭaka [SuttaCentral]. The title indicates an analysis crossing the "defilements cluster" (*kilesagocchaka*) with the wholesome triad (*kusalattika*) within the Paṭṭhāna's systematic conditional matrix [SuttaCentral].

No external parallels in Chinese, Tibetan, or Sanskrit corpora are recorded by SuttaCentral, and DharmaNexus identifies no cross-language matches scoring 10 or above [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus]. However, computational analysis via DharmaNexus indicates extensive internal Pali text reuse characteristic of the Abhidhamma's combinatorial method, finding 2,139 matching passages shared with 116 other Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its closest internal alignments include structurally neighboring chapters of the *Paṭṭhāna*, such as *Piṭṭhiduka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.13), *Parāmāsagocchaka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.9), *Upādānagocchaka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.11), *Saraṇaduka, Tika* (Patthana 3.14), *Nīvaraṇagocchaka, Kusalattika* (Patthana 3.8), and the inverted combination *Kusalattika, Kilesagocchaka* (Patthana 4.6) [DharmaNexus].
